2027-03-04.title: Thursday of the Third Week of Lent
readings: This is the nation that did not obey the voice of the Lord their God
If today you hear his voice, harden not your hearts
If it is by the finger of God that I cast out demons, the kingdom of God has come to you. Whoever is not with me is against me
2027-03-04.alt: Lenten weekday. The Alleluia is omitted throughout Lent; the Gloria is omitted except on solemnities and feasts. Liturgical colour: violet. On any weekday of this third week, especially where there are catechumens, the Mass of the Samaritan woman may be used instead: Exodus 17:1–7; Psalm 95; John 4:5–42. Commemoration of St Casimir (its collect may be used).
2027-03-04.verse: But if it is by the finger of God that I cast out the demons, then the kingdom of God has come to you.
theo: Jeremiah's words today are among the saddest in the prophets. God reminds his people of the one thing he asked when he brought them out of Egypt: “Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and you shall be my people.” But “they did not obey or incline their ear”; they followed “the stubbornness of their evil will” and “looked backward rather than forward.” Day after day God sent his prophets, and day after day they stiffened their necks. Then comes a hard sentence for Jeremiah himself: “You shall call to them, but they will not answer you.” And the final verdict: “truth has perished; it is cut off from their lips.” The Psalm turns this history into an invitation for today: “O that today you would listen to his voice! Do not harden your hearts, as at Meribah.” The hardened heart is not one that has never heard; it is one that has heard many times and stopped listening.

In the Gospel Jesus heals a man who could not speak. The crowd is amazed; but some say he does it “by Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons,” and others demand a sign from heaven. It is the same hardness Jeremiah lamented: they see the work of God and call it the work of the devil. Jesus answers with plain sense: a kingdom divided against itself cannot stand. Then the decisive word: “if it is by the finger of God that I cast out the demons, then the kingdom of God has come to you.” The “finger of God” recalls Exodus, where Pharaoh's magicians admitted that the plagues were “the finger of God,” though Pharaoh's heart stayed hard. Jesus is the “one stronger” who overpowers the strong man and frees his captives. There is no neutral ground: “Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.” Today the Church remembers St Casimir (1458–1484), a prince of Poland and Lithuania who chose Christ over the glories of court: he prayed long hours, loved the poor, kept chastity, and was devoted to the Mother of God. He died of tuberculosis at twenty-five and is the patron of Lithuania. He listened to the voice of God in a palace full of other voices.
outline: Ask: is there a voice of God you have heard many times and stopped listening to?
Point 2 · Today, harden not your hearts
The danger of the deaf heart.
The stronger one who sets captives free.
“Whoever is not with me is against me.”
live: Spend ten minutes in silence with today's Gospel and ask: what is the Lord saying to me?
Do one thing today that builds up the parish or family rather than scattering it: a word of peace, help with a task, an invitation to prayer.
2027-03-04.prayer: Lord God, you have spoken to us again and again through your prophets and in your Son. Soften our hearts so that today we may hear your voice; free us from every power of evil by the finger of your Spirit; and through the prayers of St Casimir keep us faithful to you amid the noise of the world. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: The stronger one who overpowers the strong man gives himself to us at the altar. Each Holy Communion is a victory of Christ over the evil one in us, if we open our hearts to him.

quick: Jeremiah lamented a people who would not listen to God's voice.
Jesus cast out demons by the finger of God: the kingdom has come.
St Casimir, a young prince, chose Christ and the poor over the glory of court.
2027-03-04.action: Spend ten minutes in silence with the Gospel today, asking God to speak.
2027-03-04.question: Where has my heart become hard to God's voice because I have heard it so often?
kidsaint: A prince in Poland long ago. He lived in a palace, but he did not care for fine clothes or parties. He loved to pray, he gave to the poor, and he loved Mother Mary very much. He died young, at twenty-five. Lesson: you can love Jesus most, wherever you live.

family.explain: Jesus healed a man who could not speak. Some people said: he did it with the devil's power! But Jesus said: I do it with the power of God. When Jesus is here, God's kingdom is here, and the bad things must go away.
family.intention: We pray for people who are trapped by bad habits, that Jesus may set them free.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one way our family can listen to God's voice together this week?”

illus: A schoolteacher in Kannur kept an old alarm clock on her desk that rang every morning at six. For years she pressed it off and went back to sleep, until one day she found she no longer heard it at all. She told her Lenten prayer group: that clock is like my conscience. I had heard God's call to pray so many times that I stopped hearing it. So she moved the clock across the room. This Lent she gets up, walks over, and prays.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, stronger than every evil, open our ears and soften our hearts to hear your voice today. Amen.
share: Obey my voice, and I will be your God (Jeremiah 7:23). Where am I not listening?
O that today you would listen to his voice! Do not harden your hearts (Psalm 95:7–8). What makes my heart hard?
Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters (Luke 11:23). Am I gathering or scattering?
pm.resp: If today you hear his voice, harden not your hearts.
interc: For all who preach God's word, that people may hear and not harden their hearts.
For those bound by addiction, fear or occult practices, that Christ may set them free.
For young people in places of wealth and power, that like St Casimir they may choose Christ.
For the people of Lithuania and Poland, through the prayers of St Casimir.
For our group, that we may gather with Christ and not scatter.
pm.close: Father, by the finger of your Spirit you set captives free. Make us gather with your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, God says through Jeremiah: obey my voice, and I will be your God, and you shall be my people (Jeremiah 7:23). But they did not listen. They looked backward rather than forward. And at the end: truth has perished; it is cut off from their lips.

The Psalm turns this into a word for us: O that today you would listen to his voice! Do not harden your hearts (Psalm 95:7–8). A hard heart is not one that never heard God. It is one that heard him many times and stopped listening.

In the Gospel Jesus frees a man who could not speak, and some say: he does it by Beelzebul. Jesus answers: if it is by the finger of God that I cast out the demons, then the kingdom of God has come to you (Luke 11:20). He is the stronger one who overpowers the strong man. And there is no neutral ground: whoever is not with me is against me.

Today we remember St Casimir, a young prince who lived among palace voices but listened to the voice of God. He prayed, he served the poor, he loved Our Lady. He died at twenty-five, faithful. Let us ask for his prayers, so that today, not tomorrow, we may hear the Lord's voice and gather with him. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus is stronger than anything bad. He healed a man who could not talk. Today we also remember St Casimir, a prince who loved Jesus more than his palace. Let us listen to Jesus today by saying a quiet prayer!

intro: Theme: “If today you hear his voice, harden not your hearts.”
A people that would not listen, the finger of God, and the stronger one who sets us free.

sub: Truth cut off from the lips.
q: But this command I gave them, “Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and you shall be my people; and walk only in the way that I command you, so that it may be well with you.”
Everyone then who hears these words of mine and acts on them will be like a wise man who built his house on rock.
points.apply: Choose one word of God you have heard often and act on it today.

q: For he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand. O that today you would listen to his voice! Do not harden your hearts, as at Meribah,
As it is said, “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion.”
points.apply: Make a daily ten-minute silence with the Gospel of the day for the rest of Lent.

q: And the magicians said to Pharaoh, “This is the finger of God!” But Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said.
He has rescued us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son,
points.apply: Renounce aloud, as at Baptism, one specific work of the evil one in your life, and ask Christ to free you.

concl: God speaks today; the danger is a heart that has stopped listening.
Christ, the stronger one, frees us, and calls us to gather with him.
2027-03-04.resolve: Spend ten minutes daily in silence with the Gospel until Easter.
